approach:
Root cause: `producer_loop` (run/producer.rs:272-643) sends one report back for unmet criteria, unchanged files, replay, gate, mirror drift, scope and changelog. It never runs Athena's configured checks (fmt, clippy, test), which run only in `check_and_verify` (run/mod.rs:1865). So a failing gate or an unmet command criterion is first seen by the verifier and costs the whole job.

Fix, at that origin and in the one existing send-back: after each producer report and the formatter, if a send-back can still be spent, a new `Athena::pre_verdict_checks` (run/checks.rs) runs the capability's configured checks on the producer's work tree through `run_check`. Results pass through a new `split_failures` (send_back.rs). It keeps only new, real failures. It drops checks already failing on the job's base (`verify::is_pre_existing` against `closing.baseline` filtered to `ctx.prediction`, as mod.rs:2127-2130 does) and checks killed at their deadline (`checks::timed_out`), the two cases the verdict excuses (verify.rs:447; mod.rs:2139-2158).

Each kept failure joins `problems` and the brief through `append_failed_checks`: command, exit status, output tail. The attempt invocation's `detail` stores a short note (`pre-verdict checks on the work tree: fmt ok · clippy FAILED · test ok`) on every pass the checks ran, passing or failing, so the stored record shows the check ran before the verdict. No new loop or limit: the failure shares the `PRODUCER_SEND_BACKS = 1` send-back (or the scope slot when that applies). Nothing is refused, so the share of past accepted readings newly refused is 0%.

Answers to the six findings:
(1) Pre-existing and deadline-killed runs are filtered out, with tests.
(2) The dependents list now covers every non-PASSES check in the athena-core and athena-cli tests. MARKS_BASELINE_OUTSIDE is changed to touch its marker only when run in `baseline`.
(3) A passing run stores its note on the attempt invocation, with no UI line and no new invocation.
(4) The run is skipped when no send-back is left, so no full suite runs only to make a flag.
(5) The producer.md target is named: a net change of 0 bytes, so the file stays at 1102 bytes.
(6) The fake applies edits in order, so the last write wins (athena-agent/src/fake.rs:98-111). The repair test also asserts the final README is clean.

The pre-verdict run is advisory. Verification still re-runs everything on the verifier's snapshot and decides.

decisions.choice: Run the configured checks inside `producer_loop` after each report (once the formatter has run and the change list is non-empty) and fold a kept failure into the existing single send-back. It uses the shared `send_backs`/`scope_send_backs` counters, `problems`, the attempt `detail`, and a brief section from `append_failed_checks`.
decisions.reason: The producer is the stage that lacks the information, and the only stage that can repair while it holds its work tree. The loop already gathers every pre-verdict problem into one send-back (producer.rs:499-643), so one more problem adds the information with no new budget. `PRODUCER_SEND_BACKS` (run/mod.rs:1591) stays 1.

rejected.option: A new repair loop after verification, or a higher PRODUCER_SEND_BACKS
rejected.why: Out of scope, and each miss still costs a verifier run, which is the failure being fixed.

rejected.option: A refusal rule that refuses a job whose report lacks per-criterion evidence
rejected.why: The request prefers giving the stage the information. The producer can be given the real check output instead, and a refusal would refuse readings.

rejected.option: Reuse the verification run's result by moving the checks earlier
rejected.why: Verification runs in the verifier's snapshot with the base's tool configuration, CI reuse, slots and a disk gate (mod.rs:1976-2092). Reusing a producer-tree result would weaken that independence.

decisions.choice: Send back only new, real failures. `split_failures(runs, usable_baseline)` drops a run when `crate::verify::is_pre_existing(run, baseline)` is true, where the baseline is `closing.baseline` filtered to `base_commit == ctx.prediction`. It also drops a run when `crate::checks::timed_out(run)` is true. Dropped runs are named in the stored note (`already failing on the base`, `killed at its deadline`). A deadline kill also gets one UI line (`precheck   <name> killed at its deadline; not sent back`). A kill-switch stop is an error through `refuse_if_stopped`.
decisions.reason: Answers finding 1. The verdict counts only `!passed && !is_pre_existing` (verify.rs:447) and holds a deadline kill as an environment stop (mod.rs:2144). Spending the one send-back on those would ask the producer to fix what it did not break. The baseline is taken before the producer in `baseline_stage` (mod.rs:1794), so `closing.baseline` is set when the loop runs.

rejected.why: Contradicts the verdict. lifecycle.rs `baseline_failure_does_not_stop_the_job` configures checks that fail on the base.

rejected.option: Stop at the first failure like `run_local` (routing.rs:182-197)
rejected.why: The send-back is single-shot, so it must carry everything the producer can fix. Every non-skipped check runs.

decisions.choice: Do not run the checks when nothing can be sent back. The run is skipped when `send_backs >= PRODUCER_SEND_BACKS` and the scope slot is not free, using the same `scope_slot_free` value that decides the limit break (producer.rs:571-573, moved up so the two cannot drift).
decisions.reason: Answers finding 4. At the limit a failure could only become a flag, and the verifier already re-runs the same checks and shows a failing one as `failed` under 'Checks Athena ran on this tree' (briefs.rs:1330-1348). D113 measured the suite at 9 to 11 minutes, so a last-pass run would add a full suite run that changes nothing. Consequence: an in-loop failure never reaches `report_problems` or `report_gaps`, and criterion 5 is met through the verifier's recorded checks.

rejected.option: Run on every pass and add the failure to report_gaps
rejected.why: Doubles check time on the last pass for a flag the recorded check results already carry.

decisions.choice: Skip the run, with one `precheck   not run: ...` line, when it cannot be truthful. The guard is a pure `pre_verdict_skip(nested, pinned, changed)`. It skips for a nested run (`self.nested.is_some()`, as checks.rs:542-545), for a pinned study (`ctx.pin_dir.is_some()`, as `format_stage` at producer.rs:179), for an empty change list (the idle-producer failure comes later), and when any changed path is check-tool configuration (`crate::admission::is_tool_config`, admission.rs:56-60).
decisions.reason: Verification replaces tool configuration (rustfmt.toml, clippy.toml, .cargo/config.toml) with the base's (verification.rs:472 `apply_base_tool_config`), so a run on the producer's tree would pass or fail differently from the verdict. The lifecycle test `relaxed_tool_configuration_does_not_relax_its_check` shows the divergence. Skipping avoids a false send-back, and the verifier decides.

rejected.option: Build a verifier-like scratch snapshot with the base tool configuration for the in-loop run
rejected.why: Needs a candidate commit and snapshot per pass, which is heavy and duplicates `verifier_snapshot`. A skip on these rare, governance-listed paths is enough.

decisions.choice: Take a `Class::Producer` slot like `loop_replay` (mod.rs:2336-2348). When the slot wait expires, print `precheck   not run: no build slot was free within build_wait_s` and return None; the kill switch is an error. Do not call `disk_gate` and do not read `check_seam`. Build in the producer's own `Side::Produce` environment. Snapshot the tree before the run and `restore_to` it after, naming any stray file in a UI line.
decisions.reason: `disk_gate` frees idle build directories, and some tests read free space keyed on `target/produce`. `check_seam` (mod.rs:1518) is read in `SnapExec::exec`, so reading it here would give seam tests a second fake run. The restore keeps a check that writes into the tree from changing the candidate (`SnapExec` does the same at checks.rs:139-142). Using `SnapExec` itself would reset the producer's tree to a prepared state it does not have.

rejected.option: Hold the job on a slot wait, as `check_and_verify` does
rejected.why: The verifier-side run still follows and holds if needed. `loop_replay` already treats a slot wait as a skip (mod.rs:2344).

rejected.option: Leave a check's side effects in the producer's tree
rejected.why: They would enter the candidate's change list.

decisions.choice: Store the event on the attempt invocation's `detail` (the existing home of the self-check text, producer.rs:552-563) on every pass the checks ran. A passing pass sets `detail = Some('pre-verdict checks on the work tree: fmt ok · clippy ok · test ok')`. A send-back pass inserts the same note before `; redacted report: `, which stays unique (run_pin_tests.rs:1707 splits on it). Print no UI line and add no invocation on a pass.
decisions.reason: Answers finding 3 and the accepted reading ('a stored event showing the check ran'). `Invocation.detail` (athena-data records.rs:768) is `Option<String>` with no doc comment. Producer.rs:559 already stores the self-check there, and no new field or schema is added, so no round-trip test moves. I read the code that reads an invocation `detail`. The readers at producer.rs:380 and :392 read the record before the note is set, and only for non-success outcomes. disk.rs:573 `producer_stop_reason` likewise reads failed-run detail, and audience.rs:291, auditor.rs:403, hestia.rs:2892, steward.rs:1309 and pin.rs:479 read their own role's detail. None treats a Success invocation's detail as a failure. A UI line or an extra invocation would break the 8-line, seq 1/2/3 order test (tests.rs:1068); this does not.

rejected.why: Leaves the stored record unable to show the check ran, which the reading asks for.

rejected.option: A new `pre_verdict` field on the Invocation record
rejected.why: Changes the record schema and round-trip tests for something the existing field already carries.

decisions.choice: The UI label of the in-loop lines is `precheck   `, not `checks     `.
decisions.reason: Tests find the verification line with `starts_with('checks     ')` (tests.rs:4405-4410, 4452, drain.rs:3180). An in-loop line with that label would be found first and break them. Lines print only on a skip, a deadline drop, a stray-file restore or the existing `producer   sent back:` line.

rejected.option: `checks     in the loop:` (the label in the previous plan)

decisions.choice: Hold the producer prompt set at its computed size by a net change of 0 bytes in `producer.md` (stays 1102 bytes), so `docs/system-facts.md` is not edited.
decisions.reason: The facts line `budget producer: 1043 of 1200` is compared for equality (budgets.rs:109-114). The estimator is ceil(bytes/3) (lib.rs:74-76), so 1043 means the composed set is 3127 to 3129 bytes. I could not measure where in that window it sits with read-only tools, so only a net-zero edit is guaranteed to stay equal. The bullet 9 text and the trims below are my hand counts (an estimate); the producer confirms them with `cargo test -p athena-cli --test budgets`. Bullet 9 becomes: `- Run targeted tests (`cargo test -p <crate> <filter>`) while you work. Athena runs fmt, clippy and the suite on your tree before the verifier and sends a failure back once; run the suite at most once. List in `checks_run` only checks you ran.` That is about +41 bytes. Pay for it with trims such as ` while you work` (15), `with ` in `finish, with no placeholders` (5), and `and in your brief` shortened in the last line (18), then adjust one or two bytes by punctuation. Keep the anchors 'governance file', 'stop and report it in open_issues; do not edit it', 'Never mark a requirement row Covered', 'criteria_check', and exactly one 'if docs/agent-reference.md exists in the working copy' (lib.rs:468-478, 564-651). PRODUCER_FRAME's version stays 1.

rejected.option: Update the `budget producer:` line in docs/system-facts.md
rejected.why: Not a listed deliverable; a same-size edit makes it unnecessary.
A budget never rises to fit a set (lib.rs:177-179).

decisions.choice: The decision entry is D182, appended after D181 (decisions.md:5227). It amends D113 only. It states the root cause, the 0% refusal share, that the pre-verdict run is advisory, and the trade-off: one more full suite run per job on the first pass, against a miss costing the whole job. A [[link]] (older D113, newer D182, status amended) in decision-links.toml has its `line` set to the line of the amend phrase.
decisions.reason: D113 (decisions.md:2659-2671) says the one send-back is for unmet or unreported criteria only and that the producer need not run the suite because Athena runs it on the candidate; both change in meaning. D103 is not amended because a check failure no longer enters `report_gaps` (decision 3). The log is append-only, so past entries are not edited.

rejected.why: Append-only log; edits to past entries are out of scope.

risks.risk: The full `cargo test` now runs in the loop on the first pass, so every job pays a second suite run (D113 measured 9 to 11 minutes) and a build slot. The test check never skips, so a docs-only change also runs it (athena.toml:103-108).
risks.mitigation: It builds in the producer's own warm `Side::Produce` directory, is bounded by `check_timeout_s` and a build slot, and runs only while a send-back can still be spent, so at most twice per job and never on the limit pass. D182 states the trade-off. The accepted reading chose it.

risks.risk: The producer's tree can differ from the verifier's snapshot, so a check could pass or fail differently from the verdict.
risks.mitigation: The run is advisory and the verifier decides. Tool-configuration changes (the only files the verifier replaces) skip the run with a UI line. Pre-existing and deadline-killed failures are not sent back. The brief and D182 say the run is on the work tree.

risks.risk: Existing tests with a real failing check now get one extra producer invocation, which moves counts and seqs.
risks.mitigation: I read the tests that use FAILS_ON_EDIT, leaked checks, MARKS_BASELINE_OUTSIDE and the lifecycle and drain checks, and none asserts a producer count that moves. The producer runs `cargo test -p athena-core`, `cargo test -p athena-cli --test lifecycle` and `cargo test -p athena-cli --test drain` and fixes any count I missed.

risks.risk: The slot-wait skip (no free build slot within `build_wait_s`) has no end-to-end test, since holding every slot in a test is costly.
risks.mitigation: The code copies `loop_replay`'s pattern (mod.rs:2341-2348), which the slot tests already cover. The skip prints one UI line and never holds the job. The producer runs `cargo test -p athena-core slots` to confirm none holds every slot while a job runs through the producer stage.

risks.risk: A check that writes into the work tree would put files in the candidate.
risks.mitigation: `pre_verdict_checks` restores the tree to its pre-run state and names stray files in a UI line. `pre_verdict_a_check_that_writes_into_the_tree_leaves_the_change_list_as_the_producer_left_it` tests it.

risks.risk: Holding the producer set at 1043 tokens takes a net 0-byte edit, and my hand counts of the bullet and the trims could be off by a byte or two.
risks.mitigation: The target is the file size, 1102 bytes. The budgets test prints the computed size on failure, so the producer adjusts punctuation until `system_facts_budgets_match_computed` passes with docs/system-facts.md unchanged.

risks.risk: The accepted criteria could be read as limiting which files may change, which would send a file outside the deliverables back.
risks.mitigation: None of the accepted criteria matches the limiting forms (briefs.rs:137-167), and the plan touches only the 11 listed deliverables.
